observation.visible_scene: A clear glass bottle bearing a white 'green tea milk' label stands on a pale marble-like surface. A thin stream of white milk pours continuously into the open neck from above (the pouring source is never shown). The bottle already contains a layer of dark green liquid at the bottom with white milk filling above it. A handwritten-style caption '차가운 우유 440ml / Cold milk' sits on the left, and a 'J / Dessert' logo is fixed at the top right.
visible_changes: The white milk level inside the bottle rises gradually over the first part of the clip while the green layer stays at the bottom, the two remaining largely separated.
The left 'Cold milk' caption disappears around the middle of the segment (after the ~1.5s frames).
From roughly the 2.0s frames onward a translucent duplicate of the same bottle appears offset to the upper right — an editing cross-dissolve/overlay, not a physical second object.
After that overlay the contents read as a uniform pale green (milk and green tea blended), and the framing tightens/shifts so the label is more centered and the bottle occupies more of the frame.
The milk stream at the top persists throughout the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: What caused the green and white layers to mix into a uniform color (e.g., shaking or an additional pour) is not shown.
The beginning and end of the pouring lie outside the excerpt; the stream is already flowing at the first frame and still flowing at the last.
The source of the milk stream (hand, pitcher, etc.) is never visible.
uncertain_details: Whether the later uniform-green appearance reflects true in-bottle mixing or a different shot/angle after the transition is not fully determinable.
Exact camera behavior (zoom vs. cut) is hard to confirm; the background texture shifts only slightly.
